text:
isabel: quick note — new dev who followed the sample app guide hit CI / local mismatch. local dev (node18) passes but GitHub Actions matrix (node20) fails with vitest complaining about ESM mock shape and our auth retry tests flaking.

derek: classic. did they run the sample app with `npm link` or alias to src? that hides published exports.

isabel: they followed README and used `pnpm link ../sdk` during onboarding. also sample tests use a mixture of `require()` helpers and ESM imports in different files.

morgan: linking to src is convenient but dangerous — it bypasses package.json exports and conditional `edge` entry points. For reliable CI/dev parity, recommend running `pnpm install` against the published dist tarball or a local `npm pack` artifact. Add that to onboarding docs.

julia: error snippet they pasted: 
```
TypeError: (0, _auth.getToken) is not a function
at Object.<anonymous> (/home/runner/work/repo/test/auth-retry.test.ts:12:15)
```

zane: that error often means the module shape is `export default` but consumer expects named export. Or mock replaced the shape. How are mocks written?

isabel: some tests use `vi.mock('@our/sdk/auth', ()=>({ getToken: ()=> 'x' }))` and others use `vi.mock('@our/sdk/auth', async ()=> { const actual = await vi.importActual('@our/sdk/auth'); return {...actual, getToken: vi.fn(()=> 'x')} })`. inconsistent.

derek: inconsistent mocks + link-to-src + mixed require/import will produce intermittent shape issues. Also Node 20 and Vite resolvers changed how package.exports conditions are prioritized.

morgan: propose checklist: 1) sample app onboarding: stop recommending `pnpm link` to src, show `npm pack` flow; 2) update sample repo to use ESM-only test helpers (rename setup files to .mjs or use package.json type:module); 3) provide canonical vi.mock example for auth that works with both ESM and CJS consumers.

julia: here's a minimal vi.mock pattern that preserved shape across runners: 
```
vi.mock('@our/sdk/auth', async () => {
  const mod = await vi.importActual('@our/sdk/auth');
  return { __esModule: true, ...mod, getToken: vi.fn(async () => 'fake-token') };
});
```

zane: adding `__esModule: true` can help compatibility for some bundlers but be careful — it's a shim, not a real module system fix. Prefer converting test helpers to ESM.

isabel: also onboarding friction: the quickstart sample app had vitest.config.ts aliasing `@our/sdk` -> '../sdk/src' for convenience. I'm going to remove that alias and add a note why (mismatched module resolution in CI).

derek: for CI stabilization, add a small `resolution-check` job that runs two commands in the matrix: 
```
node -e "console.log('require->', (() => { try { return require('@our/sdk/auth'); } catch (e) { return e.message } })())"
node -e "import('@our/sdk/auth').then(m=>console.log('import->', Object.keys(m))).catch(e=>console.log('import-err', e.message))"
```
This prints what resolver picks in each env.

morgan: and update package.json `exports` to include explicit small cjs shims under `./auth.cjs` during publish if too many downstreams still use require(). That buys time for migration. Open an SDK issue for that.

julia: small DX bug: our test template used `transformIgnore` that skipped node_modules including the linked package. When folks link to src it bypasses transforms, so recommend using `transformInclude` for local dev or avoid linking.

isabel: action items I'm taking: 1) update sample app README to prefer `npm pack` and include a quick resolver-check snippet; 2) remove the `@our/sdk` alias from sample vitest config; 3) add canonical vi.mock example to dev docs; 4) open SDK issue to add cjs shim for auth exports.

derek: I'll draft the PR for README+vitest config. I can also add a CI `resolution-check` job template in .github/workflows for us to reuse.

ci-bot: requested workflow run: add-resolver-check (node 18/20 matrix)

zane: note for SDK team: consider adding an `exports` entry for `./auth.node.cjs` pointing to a CJS wrapper that `module.exports = require('./dist/cjs/auth.js')` so legacy `require()` consumers don't hit ESM files. That avoids mysterious `Cannot use import statement outside a module` errors in mixed test suites.

morgan: +1. Also add a short onboarding note: "If your tests mix require() and import, convert helpers to import or pin tests to node18 while migrating."

julia: TL;DR: root cause was onboarding guidance suggesting `link` + the sample alias -> hides package exports; combined with mixed mock patterns and require() helpers produced flaky ESM/CJS resolution in CI. Fixing sample app and docs + ESM-first helpers should fix most of these pain points.

isabel: thanks all — will open PRs and link here. ping me if you hit other flakes.
